title: The Deception of the Enemy and the Flight from God
english: It is said. If these things are accomplished well while praising God, he says, 'Lord, Lord, who is like you?'; but if they should sin and turn away through which [sin] works according to malice, casting away all harmony and unity, they are scattered not just anywhere, but in the place of the dead souls.

But this has not arisen from inattention alone, but it is also possible for the eyes of the soul to be lifted toward the Lord, who is able to gather together into himself the things scattered by the adversary, interpreted as 'bones to each one,' and as the Scripture says, 'to each one' [giving] back to its own harmony. And also, to speak in the plural regarding the dispersion (for 'our bones were scattered'), while the saving [thing] is spoken of in the singular; for it is not said, 'O Lord, Lord, our eyes are toward you,' but 'my eyes.' For when the spirit of unity is toward the Lord for those seeing toward him, but malice and the dispersion of the bones is a multitude, those experiencing these things say.

Compare this also to the first commandment of God toward Adam, which had the singular regarding the command and the plural regarding the prohibition: 'For the Lord God commanded Adam, saying, From every tree of the garden you may eat, but from the tree of the knowledge of good and evil you shall not eat; for in the day that you eat of it you shall surely die' (Gen 2:16-17). And if in the Decalogue both the commands and prohibitions were expressed in the singular, the things spoken of are not invalidated; for these things will find their own proper interpretation in due time.

Toward you, O Lord, are my eyes, hoping in you; therefore do not let my soul fall, lest it fall down to the pit (Ps 140:8). For even if the bones of each of us were scattered by the adversary, yet I do not hope that you will gather and restore them to their own concord and harmony; if it does not happen by your goodness, not only will my soul not be destroyed, but it will be saved, you guarding me from the snare in which he established it for me. And not from this alone, but also from the stumbling blocks of those working lawlessness, guard me. And perhaps one snare being set for me is the deception of the wicked according to pseudo-orthodoxy, and the other is the stumbling block of those working lawlessness.

And moral wickedness, for the one stumbling in uncertainty, sees many more acting lawlessly; the testimony of this is 'For when iniquity has increased, love will flee' (Ps 140:10), and the proof is also that the trap set deceitfully, the pseudonymous one, is known from the fact that they 'strengthened themselves with a word of evil' and narrated how to hide traps.

If it is spoken concerning the devil, the explanation will be this: the enemy of our race holds a two-edged sword, woven from his various thoughts, all of which are terrible for the purpose of deceiving, which surrounds men and brings them into a fall through sin, so that they are immediately proven sinners, except for those alone who escape him. For we do not ignore his thoughts; indeed, he has caught many and is making them god-makers with nets, which he used as a snare and incense for the two-edged sword for the hunting of the deceived, as it is written in the prophet. But even if sinners fall into his two-edged sword, I, having withdrawn from all material things, am alone, so that when I pass through this timely life, I may escape the multitude of evils and be joined to the Lord, to be with Him in spirit.

No one recognizes the wise of material things and the foolish, since concerning the wise and wisdom they do not even have a concept, but only the wise recognize themselves and their neighbors. 'Since,' he says, 'no one recognizes me,' I have perceived into the right things which I previously looked upon, having had a perception of them, that since something more wise than I has come to be, my heart would come into the right side, perceiving nothing sensible but all things intelligible.

And since everyone who sins flees from God, as it is presented that one who is after transgression is said to 'flee from the face of God,' both Adam and his wife (Gen 3:8); but he who no longer sins but having been made upright speaks 'Flight has perished from me,' that is, wickedness has perished from me, in which those fleeing from God hide. Therefore also there is no one seeking my soul, having been revealed to God and having stood before Him. And 'searching out' indicates an intensification of the search: 'the one searching out'—the lost is sought and is being sought. The same thing is to have perished and to have fled. And he who has come to be in wickedness does not even repent.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: Justification through Faith and the Nature of the Soul
english: having joined my prayer

By the grace through the faith of Jesus Christ, having the righteousness that was revealed apart from law, being testified to by the law and the prophets. Perhaps, since the one believing in him is not judged, he receives from him perfect faith so that he might happen not to be judged. For judgment comes to those who loved the darkness more than the light or to those who do evil works. Surely, if God listens to someone in his own righteousness, he does not enter into judgment with him; for he happens to be his servant, doing all these things commanded to him (Ps 142:3b–4a).

To be brought low to the earth is to have the life of someone observing the things below and thinking the things upon the earth. Just as the life of those having their heart in heaven is tossed about and lifted up, so the one hoarding on the earth and having his mind about sensible things is brought low, having his life toward the earth.

He says, 'In the dark ages' (the rulers of this darkness rule there), 'as the fallen one, to be made like the dead of the age.' But those called sons of this age are not, except the one having stripped himself of these things, not a dead of the age, but having become as a dead of the age. Therefore also the spirit called the spirit of man, being with him, despaired for the sake of help. For since he has encountered the man helping him among those things, it is fitting that he despaired and was angry only upon knowing the things of the man.

This parched earth and the adjacent souls, parched places, the unclean spirit does not pass through, finding no rest or repose with them. But even if they happen to be parched by the drying up of foul waters, they do not pursue the Lord to find him on the straight path, who will also rain upon them as a preceding rain and as a dry rain. Therefore they shall be in waters, having springs in them of living water changing into eternal life.

And since the Holy Spirit does not remain where sin is, having said, 'The enemy pursued my soul' (Ps 142:3), and the following, let him be careful not because of these things to abandon him then as a spirit present with him, as it is the same as the one proposed: 'Turn not your face away,' and the Holy Spirit.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: Learning the Divine Will
english: Do not drive me away from you. For no one who is in God and possesses the Spirit is immediately cast out for sinning, but he who persists in sinning is like a craftsman preparing a tool; for then such a person will be cast out from the divine face and be deprived of the Holy Spirit. However, he who does not possess the Spirit is not stripped [of it], but he does not grieve it [while it is] present through sinning.

In the beginning of the day being illuminated by you, and having begun to shine like the rising of the sun, let me hear of your righteousness [Ps 142:8a]; I am not speaking about it as my own state or hearing. For then, having been benefited by the hearing about it, I will be able to progress as to seeing it with longing. I shall also obtain the vision of it, as he who calls to all the zealous ones, saying, 'Show us, Lord, your mercy'; for then it becomes visible, so that if someone receives what is heard, it is not in ignorance but in the beginning of knowledge, which he revealed through the First.

Perhaps also the former ways, Moses and the prophets, having been walked by someone according to 'Stand in the ways and ask for the paths of the Lord eternal' [Ps 119:58], after the journey in them, seeking the good way, he will say to the father of this [way] alone to the one knowing the way, 'Like a son, make known to me the way in which I shall walk.' Therefore also, having been acknowledged by the father, making itself manifest, he says to the worthy, 'I am the way; for no one comes to the Father except through me' [John 14:6].

Being pursued by a single enemy, as if being finished, he prays now to be rescued from a multitude of enemies [Ps 142:9]. But they do not fight with different words; for he called the leader of evil, the enemy, singular, but his army he called enemies in the plural. And it is most just to be rescued from the enemies, since he fled to no one but to him alone.

'Teach me,' he says, 'not only to know but also to do your will' [Ps 142:10]; for it is not the knowing of it that is sanctifying and making blessed, but it being worked and being done. Therefore also the Savior says, 'Not everyone saying to me, Lord, Lord, will enter the kingdom of heaven, but he who does the will of my Father' [Matt 7:21].

Regarding the one in the heavens. It is evident what one does the will of God and understands it, not necessarily being one who knows it and does not do it; for this reason, the 'Learn to do good' agrees. And what is this learning of the divine will, the following word signifies: what is the guidance of the Holy Spirit into the straight land. For the one having learned the will of God in moral virtues will be guided by the gift of God by the Holy Spirit who works upon all truth. And the straight land is the good and pure heart in which Jesus will bear fruit, the seed of the gentle ones. And it can also be thus: 'Teach me to do your will,' not merely formally but spiritually, fulfilling your law, which happens to be not other than your will; and having progressed to this and having been guided by the Holy Spirit into the straight land, one articulates the remaining truth face to face.

In some [texts] it is carried instead of 'Your Holy Spirit' as 'Your Good Spirit'; from which it is presented that the holy is good and the good is holy, and 'good' is not by participation in goodness but is good by essence, such as also the holy is. And such is the Father; for indeed it is said concerning him, 'Holy Father,' and 'No one is good except God.' And the Son, being from the good and the holy, is said to be good and holy. Ps 142:11: 'For the sake of your called name, I will do your justice. You will make me live in your righteousness, for you justify me; for it will not happen that I live in it.' It is fitting, therefore, that 'You will make me live' inclines toward future time, since here, just as we possess other good things only partially, we shall live perfectly when Christ, our life, is revealed; for he is the righteousness of God, in whom the one who approaches him will live. Ps 143:1: Since everything that is good and useful comes from God to men, what do the saints possess concerning such things? They give thanks to God, knowing him to be the cause of the good things. Behold, even David, having experienced fighting his enemies in military matters, those invisible diverse ones who are overturned and cast down, bless God, becoming a teacher to himself of that knowledge.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.
